highlights: £1.9 billion of Level C collateral was pledged on Aug 18, the highest weekly total since March 2020.
The BoE accepted loan‑backed securities that the ECB has barred from its own collateral framework.

global_commodities_price_setting_ambitio.headline: Indonesia’s New Commodities Exchange May Undermine Investor Interest
global_commodities_price_setting_ambitio.summary: Indonesia plans a commodities exchange to set global prices for its resources, but analysts warn it could deter investors and push buyers toward more liquid markets.
highlights: The exchange is slated to launch by early next year according to President‑candidate Prabowo
Analysts say forced price‑setting may drive investors to alternative venues with deeper liquidity
Malaysia’s benchmark exchange retains advantage due to transparent rules and strong foreign participation

reconsideration_of_five_year_jumbo_bond_.headline: Philippines Delays Jumbo Bond Sale Amid Soaring Inflation and Weak Peso
reconsideration_of_five_year_jumbo_bond_.summary: The government is postponing its planned five‑year jumbo bond issuance as inflation spikes and the peso weakens, raising borrowing costs.
highlights: National Treasurer Sharon Almanza said the decision will be announced soon
The original plan was prepared in June before the Middle East situation escalated

remittance_rule_ease.headline: Bangladesh Bank loosens remittance rules for Hi‑Tech Park firms
remittance_rule_ease.summary: Bangladesh Bank issued a circular allowing Hi‑Tech Park enterprises to pay royalties, technical know‑how and assistance fees from their taka accounts without prior central bank approval.
highlights: AD banks can process outward remittances from taka accounts for HTP firms
Prior approval from BHTPA remains required for payments exceeding prescribed limits

annual_loss_warning.headline: Crest Nicholson Warns of £10 Million Operating Loss as UK Homebuilder Slumps
annual_loss_warning.summary: Crest Nicholson announced an expected operating loss of about £10 million, cutting its home‑completion target to 1,350‑1,400 units amid weakening sales.
highlights: Shares fell more than 13% to a record low
Annual profit forecast reversed to a loss
Sales pace slowed over the past six weeks

rmg_factory_closures_3yrs.headline: Over 400 RMG Factories Shut Down in Bangladesh Amid Global Headwinds
rmg_factory_closures_3yrs.summary: More than 400 garment factories closed between July 2023 and June 2026 as rising costs, energy shortages and geopolitical tensions squeezed Bangladesh’s RMG sector.
highlights: 282 BGMEA and 120 BKMEA factories closed
Government offers up to 3% cash incentives and special export incentives to retain buyers
Bangladesh aims to attend 50 trade fairs in FY27 to diversify markets

cvc_10bn_secondaries_fund.headline: CVC Capital Partners Secures $10 Billion for Record‑Size Secondary Fund
cvc_10bn_secondaries_fund.summary: CVC Capital Partners announced the closing of a $10 billion Secondary Opportunities Fund VI, its largest ever fund for buying and selling private‑equity assets.
highlights: Fund size reaches $10 billion, surpassing previous records
Predecessor vehicles raised $5.8 billion in 2023 and $2.7 billion in 2019
Targets the secondary market for private‑equity asset transactions

offshore_deposit_collateral_policy.headline: Bangladesh Bank expands collateral use of OBU foreign currency deposits
offshore_deposit_collateral_policy.summary: Bangladesh Bank's new circular permits private and non‑resident foreign‑currency balances held in Offshore Banking Units to secure a wider range of local‑currency loans for residents and NRBs.
highlights: Balances in private and non‑resident foreign‑currency accounts can now back short‑term working capital, finance and consumer
The change builds on FE Circular No 27 (July 2025) and aligns with the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and GFET guidelines.

mongolia_fuel_crunch_russia.headline: Mongolia Faces Higher Fuel Prices as Russia Tightens Export Restrictions
mongolia_fuel_crunch_russia.summary: Mongolia is coping with a $1.5‑$2 per litre rise in gasoline and diesel costs after Russia’s fuel export ban, though the ban spares Mongolia.
highlights: Fuel prices in Mongolia rose by up to $2 per litre due to Russia’s supply constraints
Russia’s fuel export ban excludes Mongolia, keeping diesel shipments up 7% year‑to‑date
July fuel exports fell month‑on‑month, prompting longer queues at Mongolian petrol stations

bankresolutionact_amendment.headline: Bangladesh Scraps Bank Resolution Act Clause Allowing Ex‑Shareholders to Reclaim Control
bankresolutionact_amendment.summary: The Finance Minister introduced an amendment to repeal Section 18(a), ending a controversial mechanism that let former shareholders regain ownership of banks under resolution.
highlights: Section 18(a) permitted shareholders to apply to Bangladesh Bank for the bank’s shares, assets and liabilities.
The amendment was sent to the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance for review, with a two‑day reporting deadline.

prefinanceloan_disbursement.headline: Bangladesh Bank to Disburse 25% of Pre‑Finance Loans This Month
prefinanceloan_disbursement.summary: Bangladesh Bank Governor Mostaqur Rahman announced that 25% of low‑cost pre‑finance loans will be released this month, targeting agriculture and SMEs, with full rollout by December and economic impact expected next year.
highlights: 25% of pre‑finance scheme funds will be disbursed this month, with complete disbursement by December
The scheme prioritises agriculture and small‑medium enterprises in rural areas
Bangla QR merchants have risen from about 8 lakh at launch to 32 lakh now

directlisting_talks.headline: BSEC seeks direct listings from top local and foreign firms
directlisting_talks.summary: The regulator aims to deepen Bangladesh’s market by allowing strong companies like Unilever and bKash to list directly without an IPO, enhancing liquidity and valuation.
highlights: BSEC approved draft Direct Listing Rules 2026 at its 1,027th meeting
Companies such as Unilever, Nestlé Bangladesh, and bKash expressed interest in direct or hybrid listings
The proposed hybrid approach combines offloading existing shares with issuing new shares for fresh capital

investment_climate_reforms.headline: Bangladesh Investment Climate Reforms Spotlighted at UNCTAD Commission
investment_climate_reforms.summary: Bangladesh's recent reforms, including faster clearances and a new unified Invest Bangladesh agency, earned UNCTAD recognition as a model for developing economies.
highlights: FDI rose 39.36% to $1.77 billion in 2025
Bangladesh merged three agencies into Invest Bangladesh to streamline investment facilitation
UNCTAD named Bangladesh among few LDCs attracting Greenfield investment in 2025

second_jamuna_padma_bridges_feasibility.headline: Bangladesh signs consultancy deal for feasibility studies of second Jamuna and Padma bridges
second_jamuna_padma_bridges_feasibility.summary: The Bangladesh Bridge Authority hired international consultants to finish a feasibility study in eight to nine months for new Jamuna and Padma bridges, enhancing regional connectivity and growth.
highlights: Study duration set at 12 months, but officials urge completion within eight to nine months
Consultancy involves firms from Nepal, Sweden, South Korea and Bangladesh
New bridges aim to ease pressure on existing road networks and boost transport efficiency

expatriate_role_investment.headline: President urges expatriates to boost investment and development in Bangladesh
expatriate_role_investment.summary: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir called on Bangladeshi expatriates, especially in the United Kingdom, to increase investment, create jobs and support social projects in Bangladesh.
highlights: Expatriates' remittances are a key driver of Bangladesh’s economy
The government introduced a “Probashi Card” to provide comprehensive services for overseas Bangladeshis
Airport harassment issues and voting rights for expatriates are being addressed

beneficial_ownership_disclosure.headline: Bangladesh to Mandate Beneficial Ownership Disclosure in Companies Act Amendment
beneficial_ownership_disclosure.summary: The government proposes mandatory disclosure of actual owners, tighter anti‑money‑laundering rules, and reduced capital thresholds for one‑person companies.
highlights: Fines up to Tk50,000 and daily penalties apply for non‑compliance with ownership reporting.
A digital platform will enable the BFIU and Anti‑Corruption Commission to access ownership data on lawful request.

textiles_jute_committee.headline: Parliament Forms New Textile and Jute Standing Committee
textiles_jute_committee.summary: The ruling party appointed Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia to lead the newly created Parliamentary Standing Committee on Textiles and Jute, expanding oversight of the ministry.
highlights: Committee chaired by Md Akhtaruzzaman Mia (Dinajpur-4)
Members include lawmakers from BNP, Jamaat, and Bangladesh Khilafat Majlis
26 of the 50 standing committees have been formed so far

ex_railway_minister_assets.headline: Court Seizes Land, SUVs, Freezes Accounts of Ex‑Railway Minister
ex_railway_minister_assets.summary: A Dhaka court ordered the attachment of 284 decimals of land, two SUVs and the freezing of six bank accounts belonging to former Railway Minister Mujibul Haque over alleged graft.
highlights: Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir approved the Anti‑Corruption Commission’s plea to seize assets
The ACC alleges Mujibul Haque acquired Tk7.39 crore beyond his known income

edible_oil_shortage_persists_prices_rema.institution: Bangladesh Ministry of Food and Disaster Management
edible_oil_shortage_persists_prices_rema.headline: Bangladesh faces persistent edible oil shortage as prices surge
edible_oil_shortage_persists_prices_rema.summary: Despite a Tk5‑per‑litre price hike, bottled soybean oil remains scarce, while sugar, eggs and vegetables continue climbing, tightening household budgets.
highlights: Bottled soybean oil price rose to Tk204 per litre, yet supply stays tight.
Sugar and key vegetables have risen Tk10‑20 per kg in the past two weeks.
A dozen eggs now costs Tk165, up from previous discounts.

berc_chairman_calls_for_updated_1996_ene.headline: Bangladesh's Energy Crisis Grim, Calls for Balanced Policy and Renewables
berc_chairman_calls_for_updated_1996_ene.summary: BERC chairman Jalal Ahmed warned that Bangladesh's reliance on imported fuel and limited domestic gas exploration leaves the nation facing a grim energy outlook requiring coordinated short‑, medium‑ and long‑term actions.
highlights: Two FSRUs are operating but four are needed, with new projects taking up to 30 months to start.
Installed generation capacity stands at about 30,000 MW versus roughly 17,000 MW demand, inflating capacity payments.
Solar power is deemed most promising, yet battery storage costs and limited sunshine hours hinder large‑scale adoption.

venezuela_oil_deal_race.headline: Trump‑linked firms scramble for Venezuela oil contracts amid sanctions
venezuela_oil_deal_race.summary: U.S. companies with ties to former President Trump are aggressively pursuing new agreements to purchase Venezuelan crude despite ongoing sanctions and political uncertainty.
highlights: Several Trump‑affiliated firms have entered negotiations with Venezuela’s state oil company PDVSA
The deals aim to secure low‑cost crude for U.S. refineries as sanctions tighten
U.S. Treasury officials warn of heightened enforcement risk for participants

finance_minister_announces_ppp_pilot_for.headline: Bangladesh Declares Clean Water a Constitutional Right, Launches PPP Pilot
finance_minister_announces_ppp_pilot_for.summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury affirmed clean water as a constitutional right and unveiled a 12‑month public‑private partnership pilot in Chattogram.
highlights: CWASA, Max Foundation Bangladesh and Nepal, and Max Social Enterprise signed a tripartite MoU for the pilot
The pilot will use IoT‑monitored systems to deliver community water services in Wards 40 and 41 without financial input from CWASA
The Netherlands Embassy will provide technical and financial support, emphasizing Dutch expertise in water management

al_madina_pharma_under_bsec_probe_for_tk.headline: BSEC probes Al-Madina Pharma over Tk41 crore receivables and sales gaps
al_madina_pharma_under_bsec_probe_for_tk.summary: The regulator has launched a formal enquiry into Al-Madina Pharmaceuticals’ 2024‑2025 accounts, focusing on Tk41 crore in receivables, sales discrepancies and audit compliance.
highlights: The three‑member BSEC team will physically verify at least ten customers linked to the receivable balances.
Al-Madina reported receivables of Tk21.13 crore for 2025, up from Tk20.12 crore in 2024.

multinational_listing_policy.headline: BSEC Chairman Urges Multinationals to List on Bangladesh Stock Market
multinational_listing_policy.summary: BSEC chief Masud Khan announced plans to compel large multinational firms to list on the Dhaka Stock Exchange within a year, using new legal tools.
highlights: BSEC will introduce a “Public Interest Company” definition to force listings if firms refuse voluntarily.
A hybrid direct‑listing model and extended audits aim to speed up IPO approvals.
Institutional investors such as pension and insurance funds will be encouraged to buy shares and corporate bonds.

global_food_price_spike.headline: World Food Prices Hit Three-Year High Amid Climate and War Risks
global_food_price_spike.summary: In August, the FAO reported the Food Price Index rose to 133.3 points, the highest since November 2022, driven by heat, El Nino and Black Sea conflicts.
highlights: Europe faces extreme heat and drought threatening maize and sugar beet harvests
Escalating attacks in the Black Sea cut grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine
Sugar benchmark jumped 11.9%, its highest since June 2025

supersized_elnino.headline: UN Warns Supersized El Niño Could Become Strongest Ever Recorded
supersized_elnino.summary: The World Meteorological Organization says a near‑certain El Niño will persist through February 2027, potentially becoming the strongest on record and driving extreme weather.
highlights: El Niño temperatures are already over 2 °C above normal, placing it in the “very strong” category.
The event threatens food security in Central America’s Dry Corridor and could affect energy and water resources worldwide.

brics_summit_participation.headline: Bangladesh’s Tarique Rahman Attendance at BRICS Summit Remains Unconfirmed, MEA Says
brics_summit_participation.summary: India’s Ministry of External Affairs confirmed there is no update on whether Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will attend the upcoming BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
highlights: No confirmation on Rahman’s participation or any alternative Bangladeshi representative
Bangladesh’s former PM Sheikh Hasina discussed conditions for her return, unrelated to the summit
China’s President Xi Jinping attendance is still pending official confirmation

labour_adviser_plan.headline: Bangladesh Govt Vows Sustainable Jobs and Safe Workplaces, Highlights Family Card Initiative
labour_adviser_plan.summary: Prime Minister’s adviser Mahdi Amin pledged to boost quality employment, empower women, and keep factories open by enhancing skills and improving labour protections.
highlights: The government launched the ‘Family Card’ programme to increase women’s participation in the garment sector.
Closed factories have been reopened and new investments attracted despite regional energy challenges.

corruption_costs_statement.headline: Bangladesh Ties Pay Rise to Asset Disclosure Amid $16 Billion Corruption Loss
corruption_costs_statement.summary: The new government proposes conditional salary hikes for officials, requiring annual wealth statements to curb corruption that drains roughly $16 billion from the economy each year.
highlights: Pay raises will apply only to officials who publish renewable asset statements
Corruption costs Bangladesh about $16 billion annually, exceeding its total foreign investment
Tax‑to‑GDP ratio remains among the world’s lowest, driven by evasion and weak enforcement

online_betting_money_laundering.headline: CID arrests four in Khulna for online betting money‑laundering scheme
online_betting_money_laundering.summary: Police detained four suspects in Khulna accused of channeling betting deposits through mobile financial services and bank accounts, converting them into cryptocurrency for overseas transfer.
highlights: Agents regularly changed MFS numbers and bank accounts to evade detection.
Funds were moved to platforms like Binance before being smuggled abroad.
Arrests were made after raids on Khan Jahan Ali and Khalishpur neighborhoods.

bus_service_halt.headline: Owner-Worker Dispute Halts Inter-District Bus Services from Rajshahi
bus_service_halt.summary: A dispute between bus owners and workers in Rajshahi and Natore triggered a district-wide shutdown, suspending inter‑district bus routes to Dhaka and Rangpur.
highlights: Three Tuhin Paribahan buses were detained in Rajshahi after a Rabbi Paribahan bus was stopped in Natore.
The Rajshahi District Motor Workers Union announced a blanket suspension of all inter‑district services from Rajshahi.
Travelers were left stranded at Rajshahi’s bus terminal with no alternative routes.

energyimportanalysis2026.headline: Bangladesh’s Shift to Imported Fuels Deepens Energy Crisis Ahead of 2030 Deadline
energyimportanalysis2026.summary: Bangladesh relies increasingly on costly imported coal, LNG and electricity as short‑term fixes replace long‑term domestic energy solutions, straining finances.
highlights: Annual coal imports exceed $1.1 billion despite domestic reserves worth up to $1.26 trillion
LNG spending has risen to $3.8 billion and may hit $8.5 billion by 2029‑30
Renewable generation reached only 2.5% of power in 2020, far below the 10% target

hospitalcorporatemodelshift2026.headline: Bangladesh Medical University to Relaunch Super Specialised Hospital under Non‑Profit Corporate Model
hospitalcorporatemodelshift2026.summary: The government will revive the Tk1,500 crore, 750‑bed Super Specialised Hospital as a non‑profit corporate entity, aiming for faster procurement and improved staffing.
highlights: BMU will hold 90% of shares, government 10%, operating as a separate company under the Companies Act.
A new board of directors will include corporate, legal and accounting experts to accelerate procurement and staffing.
Fees will be modestly higher than current rates, with any surplus reinvested to keep services affordable.
